summary: Strong Phase 1 artifact with a credible full Nord Stage 4 73 surface, exact 73-key keybed, clean runtime, and honest generated-synthesis piano source. Main gaps are simplified micro-detail, very small narrow rendering, shallow real-boundary tests, unexercised MIDI/multitouch evidence, and a basic triangle oscillator voice rather than a more piano-like source.

evidence: Runtime desktop measurement at 1440x900 showed .instrument-shell 1353.6x437.3, ratio 3.09514, matching the Stage 4 73 measured aspect ratio 3.0951 and occupying 94% viewport width.
The rendered instrument is a continuous red chassis with top/bottom rails, end cheeks, dark deck panels, and a 73-key hammer-action keybed; no desktop overflow or clipping was observed.
Deck/keybed split follows the phase audit and CSS grid rows 6% top rail, 48% deck, 41% keybed, 5% bottom rail, matching the 54/46 allocation.
Silhouette details such as rail cutouts, cheeks, shadows, and key fronts are credible but approximate rather than reference-exact.
src/hardware.ts defines the six required sections in the correct order and fractions: performance 0.13, organ 0.21, piano 0.15, program 0.09, synth 0.21, effects 0.21.
Runtime DOM contained 101 decorative controls plus 73 piano keys, with Program and Synth as the only OLED elements.

Required landmarks are present: nine organ drawbars with LED ladders, piano type/layer/detail controls, program display/dial/eight buttons/navigation/live/scene/store/split/morph controls, synth OLED and oscillator/filter/envelope/LFO/arp controls, and grouped effects controls.
The inventory captures the major hardware groups, but some tiny printed legends and exact control-density nuances from the hardware are simplified.
Desktop screenshot shows credible Nord red metal, dark blue-gray inset panels, black/white key materials, green LED ladders, glowing cyan OLEDs, knobs, faders, drawbars, and button states.
CSS uses distinct gradients/shadows for chassis, controls, OLEDs, keys, fader caps, drawbars, and wheels rather than a flat schematic.
Typography and legends are dense and hardware-like on desktop, but many labels are abbreviated, ellipsized, or too simplified to reproduce the original micro-typography exactly.
At 390x844 runtime measurement showed the complete shell retained at 374.4x121.0 with all 73 keys and 101 controls still in the DOM and no document-level overflow.
The narrow screenshot shows the full chassis/keybed and status strip visible without clipping or vertical scroll.

However, mobile control labels render at 3.4px, making panel state and legends effectively inspection-only rather than comfortably legible; the screenshot also shows a horizontal scrollbar area at the bottom.
Key buttons implement pointer down/up/cancel/lost-capture note start/end with pointerId tracking; computer keyboard mapping covers a central playable range and suppresses repeat events.
Web MIDI handling is implemented for note on/off and CC64 sustain, with unavailable/denied/no-input status reporting and disconnect cleanup.

Tests cover pointer press/cancel/blur and computer keyboard sustain, but do not directly exercise independent multitouch, MIDI note/velocity/CC64, denied MIDI via mocks, or disconnected MIDI behavior.

src/pianoEngine.ts implements velocity-scaled gain, per-note release envelopes, sustain hold/release, maxVoices=18 in the app, deterministic stealing preferring released/oldest voices, allNotesOff, and dispose cleanup.
Candidate tests use a fake AudioContext to verify noteOn/noteOff, sustain transitions, voice stealing, allNotesOff, and timer-based voice cleanup.

Repeated/overlapping same-note ownership is imperfect: visual active state is a Set keyed only by keyId, so one owner releasing a key can clear the visual state while another same key voice remains active.
No test renders or analyzes actual audio output, so velocity/release/sustain behavior is proven structurally rather than as real audible signal behavior.
IMPLEMENTATION_DETAILS.json truthfully declares live generated synthesis only, no recorded samples, and no external audio assets.
Runtime status strip reported 'Generated piano ready' and 'Audio: generated synthesis'; panel controls are explicitly labeled decorative in the UI.
Fallback status is implemented when AudioContext is missing or fails to start and is covered by a unit test.

The source is a simple triangle OscillatorNode through gain envelopes, dependable but only loosely piano-like; the no-AudioContext fallback message says playable even though no audible fallback source exists.
Every visible control is rendered as a focusable button with a stable data-control-id, accessible name, visible focus style, and keyboard support for Enter/Space/arrows/Home/End.
Runtime click on program.live-mode changed aria-pressed from false to true and added the is-active visual class while leaving piano status unchanged.
Keys expose aria-pressed and release cleanly after keyboard activation; console stayed clean during runtime interaction checks.

Knobs, faders, encoders, drawbars, and wheels move by click/keyboard increments rather than true drag gestures, and non-button controls remain role='button' with aria-valuenow instead of canonical slider-style roles.
Panel controls update only React presentation state in controlState; no decorative control is wired into the PianoEngine or other audio/system state.

UI status says 'Panel controls decorative in Phase 1', Synth OLED says 'Decorative / No synth audio', and IMPLEMENTATION_DETAILS.json explicitly states panel controls outside keybed/sustain do not change audio/program/synth/organ/effects state.
Runtime toggling a Program control changed only its visual/ARIA state and did not alter the generated piano status.
The code is reasonably separated into normalized hardware data (src/hardware.ts), React rendering/input orchestration (src/App.tsx), and a small injectable piano engine (src/pianoEngine.ts).

tests/feature-matrix.json maps every required Phase 1 feature ID to src/App.test.tsx, and the test file checks key counts, sections, OLED locations, control IDs, pointer/computer-key behavior, fallback, and fake-engine lifecycle.

Coverage is shallow for several hard gates: MIDI, denied/disconnected MIDI, independent multitouch, same-note overlap, real browser audio output, and actual responsive screenshots are not exercised by tests.
The fake AudioContext verifies node construction and cleanup mechanics but does not prove rendered signal differences, velocity response, or audible sustain/release behavior.
Reran pnpm test, pnpm typecheck, pnpm lint, and pnpm build in the sealed artifact; all passed. dist/index.html is present.
Parent capture evidence and browser runtime checks both showed no console errors/page errors during desktop and narrow inspection.
Runtime DOM remained stable under reload, decorative click, keyboard activation, and viewport changes; no stuck visual key or console error was observed.
There were pnpm bin-link warnings during install-wrapper execution, and runtime confidence is limited by lack of real audio/MIDI stress coverage.

issues: Narrow layout preserves the full instrument but renders controls and legends extremely small (3.4px labels at 390x844), limiting usable inspection and legible state.
Candidate tests do not directly exercise Web MIDI note/CC64, denied/disconnected MIDI behavior, independent multitouch, or actual audio rendering.
The generated voice is a simple triangle oscillator with envelopes; it is honest and playable but only a basic approximation of a piano-like source.
Overlapping same-key ownership is not fully represented in visual state because active keys are tracked by keyId Set rather than per input owner.
